title: Acquisition Geo Onboarding: handshake & operational runbook
body:
Purpose:
This note captures the operational and compliance considerations for onboarding a recently-acquired company ("Nimbus AI") into Redwood's private deployment/residency model. Focus: tenant region mapping, key custody transitions, evidence collection for audits, staged enablement, rollback criteria, and operator playbook.

Context & constraints:
- Nimbus has 87 tenants across EU, UK, and APAC. Their current stack uses a mix of cloud regions and a customer-specific KMS in eu-west-1.
- Target: migrate to Redwood Private control plane with minimal service disruption and auditable evidence that tenant data residency (region pin) is preserved per contract.
- Legal requirement: for 12 enterprise tenants, data must remain within EU (no cross-border backups), and KMS keys must be resident in EU HSM for 2 tenants.
- Timeline requirement: staged rollouts over 8 weeks with weekly checkpoints to legal/compliance.

High-level plan (phased):
1) Inventory & classification (Week 0–1)
   - Export tenant manifest from Nimbus: tenant-id, country, contract-residency-statement, current-kms-location, active-data-types (chat, files, embeddings).
   - Quick validation script: run checksum and sample object listing for 10% of tenants to confirm logical locality.
   - Outcome: canonical mapping csv (tenant_id, desired_region, current_region, kms_location, escalation_flag).

2) Legal & Contract alignment (concurrent with inventory)
   - Legal to confirm permitted fallback policies per tenant (soft-pin vs hard-pin).
   - Flag any tenants needing a contractual amendment for migration.

3) Prep environment & escrow (Week 1–3)
   - Create per-region escrow buckets: eu-escrow-<date>, uk-escrow-<date>, apac-escrow-<date>. These buckets are write-once, immutable for audit window.
   - For tenants with HSM requirement, provision EU HSM keys under a dedicated customer key ring. Document key IDs and operators.
   - Snapshot tests: take sample snapshot of tenant metadata (no PII) and produce an audit-hash manifest.

4) Staged activation (Week 3–7)
   - Stage A (Week 3): low-risk tenants (non-enterprise, low traffic). Enable region pin in staging environment with test traffic.
   - Stage B (Week 4–5): medium-risk tenants and those with complex storage patterns. Monitor telemetry for cache misses, latency changes, and KV cache footprint.
   - Stage C (Week 6–7): enterprise tenants behind contractual obligations, HSM migration. These require a dry-run and legal sign-off before cutover.

5) Post-cutover verification & audit packaging (Week 7–8)
   - Verify evidence: per-tenant logs showing routing decisions, storage location stamps, and KMS key usage events.
   - Package a tamper-evident audit bundle (audit_manifest.json, audit_hash.txt) and push to escrow buckets. Notify legal and customer success.

Decision knobs and fallbacks:
- Soft-pin fallback: allow burst routing to nearest compatible region for up to 5% of traffic for 10 minutes if capacity exhausted; requires customer opt-in.
- Hard-pin: strictly enforce region routing with rejection and operator alert if local capacity unavailable. Requires contractual guarantee and compensating SLA language.
- KMS dual-signature handshake: for HSM-bound tenants, require both Nimbus original key owner and Redwood platform key to sign a transfer token before rewrapping keys. If handshake fails, abort HSM migration and keep original key in place.

Operator playbook (for each tenant cutover):
- Pre-cutover checklist (run this in staging):
  1) Confirm canonical mapping row exists and status=ready.
  2) KMS check: list-key <tenant_key_id> -> ensure location matches target region.
  3) Telemetry baseline capture: latency, error_rate, cache_hit_rate (last 72h).
  4) Create ephemeral monitor channel: #acq-onboard-<tenant-id>.
  5) Reserve capacity: allocate dedicated pool or reserve burst tokens for 2 hours.

- Cutover steps (expected runtime 8–20 minutes):
  1) Toggle tenant routing flag to region=<target> in config-store (feature flag).
  2) Trigger soft-prefix cache warm (prefetch last 100 active sessions where possible).
  3) Push metrics instrumentation and start detailed trace sampling for tenant.
  4) Confirm first successful write/read anchored in target region (check storage object location header).
  5) Incrementally ramp traffic: 10% -> 50% -> 100% over 10 minutes, monitor SLOs.

- Abort / rollback criteria:
  - Latency increase > 200ms p95 above baseline for > 5 minutes.
  - Error rate > 3x baseline for > 5 minutes.
  - KMS key-signature failures or rewrap errors.
  - Evidence of data placed outside declared region.
  If any condition hits, immediately toggle routing flag back to previous_region and open an incident with SRE-runbook #region-reversion.

Telemetry & verification signals to collect:
- routing_evidence: per-request header (region_routed, region_storage_id, kms_key_id) logged to secure audit stream.
- storage_stamp: every write must include storage_region tag and persistent object manifest should surface region_id.
- kms_events: key usage, wrap/unwrap events with operator id.
- health_signals: cpu, gpu utilization per host, queue depth, tail-latencies.
- periodic evidence snapshot: run daily evidence exporter that bundles last 24h into escrow for 14 days post-cutover.

Audit packaging template (deliverable to legal/customer):
- audit_manifest.json (list of tenant ids, target_region, timestamp, evidence_bundle_id)
- evidence_bundle_<id>.tar.gz (logs, storage-manifests, KMS event snippets, audit_hash.txt)
- audit_hash.txt (sha256 sums of files + signed by ops key)

Edge cases & notes:
- Tenants with hybrid data (some historic archives stored in a different region): mark as "mixed-archive" and require an archive migration plan or an approved legal exception.
- Cross-account KMS: if Nimbus keys are managed in a partner account, schedule cross-account policy updates and ensure proper IAM principal mapping.
- Data residency vs latency tradeoffs: document explicit decisions for each tenant when soft-pin allowed.

Testing harnesses & smoke tests:
- Create a synthetic traffic driver that simulates session flows and validates storage stamps. Ticket: JIRA PD-4821.
- Chaos tests: induce a regional capacity shortage and validate fallback behaves per policy (soft vs hard).
- Regression evals: run a small eval-suite (prompt sets) to ensure model-serving results are unchanged after region switch (checks for data locality affecting model caches).

Communication & customer success steps:
- Pre-cutover email template: include expected window (2 hours), expected visible changes (none for end-user), rollback conditions, and customer contact for the window.
- Post-cutover confirmation: deliver audit bundle and short summary of telemetry comparisons vs baseline.

Open questions / outstanding decisions:
- Confirm retention window for escrow buckets (recommended 90 days but legal to confirm).
- Decide on acceptable soft-pin percentage for enterprise tenants (legal/CS approval required).
- Finalize operator escalation list and on-call shifts for cutover weeks.

Appendix: quick operator commands:
- Export tenant mapping (internal tooling): ./onboard/export_mapping --source=nimbus --out=tenant-canonical.csv
- Toggle routing flag: ./platformctl set-tenant-region --tenant=<id> --region=<region> --reason="acq-onboard"
- Sample check storage location: curl -H "X-Auth: token" https://internal-api/storage/meta/<object-id> | jq .region
- Verify KMS wrap: ./kmsctl test-wrap --key=<key-id> --tenant=<id>

Slack channels and warroom: #acq-onboard-coord, #acq-ops-escrow, #legal-acq-review

Owner notes: this is intentionally operational rather than final contractual language. Legal sign-off required before any HSM/key movement. Recommended next step: schedule a 90-minute tabletop with SRE, Legal, CS, and an infra engineer to walk through one representative enterprise tenant end-to-end.
